data.paper_title: Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects
data.selected_experiment: Table 2, Fama-MacBeth monthly cross-sectional regressions of NYSE stock returns on mean-adjusted illiquidity (ILLIQMA) and other characteristics, 1964-1997, all-months column

economic_rationale.value: Stock expected return increases in illiquidity (illiquidity premium), as proposed by Amihud and Mendelson (1986); ILLIQ proxies for price impact per dollar of volume.

universe_and_filters.value: NYSE-traded stocks (CRSP daily and monthly data), 1963-1997. A stock enters month m of year y if it has a return that month, return and volume data for more than 200 days in year y-1, is listed at the end of year y-1, has a price above $5 at the end of year y-1, has market capitalization data in CRSP, and its ILLIQ in year y-1 is not in the highest or lowest 1% tail. Returns are adjusted for delistings (Shumway, 1997).

value: end-of-year market capitalization (filter and SIZE control)
daily returns on size-decile portfolios and equally-weighted market (for BETA control)

signal_formula_words.value: For each stock and year, ILLIQ is the average over the year of the daily ratio of absolute return to dollar trading volume; it is divided by the cross-sectional mean ILLIQ of that year (ILLIQMA) and used in the next year's monthly cross-sectional regressions on stock returns.

evidence.quote: Stock illiquidity is deﬁned here as the average ratio of the daily absolute

signal_formula_symbols.value: ILLIQ_iy = (1/D_iy) * sum_{d=1}^{D_iy} |R_iyd| / VOLD_iyd; AILLIQ_y = (1/N_y) * sum_i ILLIQ_iy; ILLIQMA_iy = ILLIQ_iy / AILLIQ_y; R_imy = k_0my + sum_j k_jmy X_{j,i,y-1} + U_imy

skip_window.value: none (characteristics from year y-1 are used for returns in all months of year y)

holding_period.value: 1 month (monthly returns regressed each month of year y on characteristics from year y-1)

rebalance_frequency.value: monthly cross-sectional regressions (408 months); characteristics updated annually

breakpoints.value: none; continuous regressor in Fama-MacBeth regressions, with the extreme 1% upper and lower ILLIQ tails excluded

favored_group.value: stocks with high illiquidity (high ILLIQ / ILLIQMA)

disfavored_group.value: stocks with low illiquidity (low ILLIQ / ILLIQMA)

headline_result.value: Mean Fama-MacBeth coefficient on ILLIQMA of 0.162 (t = 6.55) for all months, 0.126 (t = 5.30) excluding January.

unresolved_details: The paper has no portfolio-sort strategy; the evidence is Fama-MacBeth regression coefficients, so no long-short portfolio, quantile cutoffs or weighting is defined.
Regressions are OLS, so stocks are implicitly equal-weighted; no value weighting is described.
Exact units/scaling of dollar volume and whether the return convention includes dividends are not detailed.
Whether results are used as a trading portfolio rule (long high ILLIQ, short low ILLIQ) is not stated.
Control variables (BETA, R100, R100YR, SIZE, SDRET, DIVYLD) differ between the two specifications in Table 2.
